This application coming on for hearing this day, the cou  following:
 ORDER With the consent, heard finally.
Perused the case diary.

This is first application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C for grant of bail to the applicant, as he has been arrested on 07.11.2022 in connection with Crime No.235/2022 registered at Police Station Tyonda, District Vidisha (M.P.) fo r commission of offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n),
Sonu Kushwah vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97467835/
1 376(3)(n), 376(d)(A), 506 of IPC, Under Section 5/6 of POCSO Act and under Sections 3(2)(v) and 3(1)(w)(ii) of SC/ST Act.
Prosecution case, in brief, is that on 06.11.2022 minor prosecutrix aged about 15-16 years, who is a member of SC/ST community made an oral complaint to police station Tyonda, District Vidisha to the effect that about eight months ago when she along with her mother went to the field of Sundarlal Soni situated at Baagrond for harvesting crops at that time she met with the applicant.

sentences.text: During the said period, the applicant with the help of co-accused Deepesh Singh took her to canal and committed sexual intercourse with her while co-accused recorded a video of aforesaid incident.
Thereafter, the applicant used to threaten her to get viral the aforesaid video and committed sexual intercourse with her, due to which she became pregnant.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the matter.
He further submits that as per prosecution case itself, FIR was lodged after about eight months of the incident without any plausible explanation.

He further submits that the prosecutrix was major at the time of incident as her aged is proved by her Samagra ID prepared on 07.08.2015 and according to which, she was 20 years of age at the time of incident.
Statements of the prosecutrix have been recoded and the same are inconsistent with the FIR and her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
Neither the mobile phone nor any video clipping has been seized in the matter.
DNA report is negative and does not support the prosecution case.
The applicant is in custody since 07.11.2022.
His custodial interrogation or trial is not required in the matter.
Co-accused has been granted bail by this Court vide order dated 13.03.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.7010/2023.
Trial will take time for its conclusion.
Hence, prayer is made to enlarge the applicant on bail.
Learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the application and submits that the prosecutrix was minor at the time of incident and as per her school register, her date-of-birth is 30.01.2007.
Specific allegations have been made against the applicant.

The offence is serious in nature,
therefore, he be not released on bail.

Having considered the rival submissions, material pointed out by learned counsel for the applicant,
specially with regard to the DNA report, so also considering the other facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail, hence, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Court for his appearance before the Trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the Trial Court during the pendency of trial.
It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437 (3) of Cr. P. C.
This application is allowed and stands disposed of.
Certified copy, as per rules.
